assumptions.text: All four contexts share one deployable (scale target 1-3, decompose N2 'modular monolith'); every cross-context message is an in-process call or an in-memory domain event. The connect inputs sheet proposed 'separate' for every relationship by keying on the wording of decompose N2; overridden here.
Minted commands discover lacks: send-due-notice (lending -> email), send-fee-notice (fees -> email), charge-card (fees -> stripe). Domain-language names; discover should adopt them on a re-run.
Stripe's asynchronous confirmation (discover N4) is folded into the charge-card response: the synchronous reply and any later webhook carry the same paymentAttemptId and the second one is a no-op.

In-memory domain events are at-most-once: if the process dies between the lending write and the fees handler, the accrual starts the next nightly run, which re-derives overdue loans from lending's state. Acceptable at this scale.
One thin Stripe adapter is shared by fees and membership (decompose N3); membership's pay-membership-fee uses the same charge-card message. Not drawn at light depth.

open_questions.text: Should discover adopt send-due-notice, send-fee-notice and charge-card as commands (they are minted here)?
Does the coordinator want a cash payment at the desk to go through pay-fee with method=cash (no Stripe call), or a separate record-cash-payment command?

notes_for_downstream.text: Sharpens decompose N3: charge-card is one shared Stripe adapter (a driven port in fees, re-used by membership for the joining fee). Nightly clock commands (mark-loans-overdue, accrue-late-fee, send-due-reminders, expire-reservations, lapse-memberships) are driving ports invoked by a scheduler, not HTTP.

Every cross-context hop is in-process on the assumption of one deployable. If organise splits the clock-driven work into a worker, loan-overdue and item-returned cross a process boundary and need an outbox; re-run connect then.

flows.name: Reserve, collect and return on time
flows.summary: A member reserves a drill online, the desk volunteer checks it out after lending confirms standing with membership and fees, a reminder goes out, and the item comes back; a damaged return hands the item to inventory.

flows.name: Late return, fee accrues, member pays by card
flows.summary: The clock marks a loan overdue; fees accrues GBP 1 a day and tells the member; the item comes back, which stops accrual; the member pays online through Stripe.

flows.name: Failed inspection becomes a damage charge; item retired
flows.summary: No discover scenario covers it: after a damaged return the maintenance volunteer inspects the item; a failure reaches the coordinator, who charges damage; the item is retired and lending stops offering it.

integration_patterns.rationale: Lending needs the answer to continue check-out (decompose D1); a synchronous in-process query at one deployable.
Same: balance is read at check-out; fees keeps its ledger private behind the query.
Fees reacts to loan-overdue and item-returned; lending needs no answer. In-memory domain events, at-most-once, re-derivable nightly (A4).
Inventory publishes item lifecycle facts (item-retired, versioned); lending subscribes and never edits condition.
A damaged return is an event inventory reacts to with a manual policy; lending does not wait for the inspection.
A failed inspection is a fact the coordinator acts on later; fees does not need inventory to wait.

coupling_concerns.text: charge-card is called inside pay-fee: an external call inside the unit of work that records the payment. A timeout after Stripe charged but before fees wrote fee-paid would double-charge without the idempotency key.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: Record the attempt first (pending), call Stripe with the attempt id as idempotency key, then record the outcome; a later webhook with the same key is a no-op.

coupling_concerns.text: Check-out waits on two synchronous reads (membership, fees); the desk hot path depends on both being up. Accepted because all three live in one process (decompose D1).
coupling_concerns.mitigation: If organise separates fees or membership, replace the reads with a subscribed standing projection (decompose D1 would_flip_if).

coupling_concerns.text: Lending and fees depend on each other: lending queries fees for the balance, fees consumes lending's loan-overdue and item-returned. Consumer-depends-on-producer both ways.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: Keep both directions to one thin message each; if it grows, fees publishes a balance-changed event and lending keeps a standing projection instead of querying.

plain_words.what: We drew who sends what to whom for three stories: a normal loan, a late loan with a fee, and a damaged tool that gets charged and retired.
plain_words.decided: 3 flows, 19 messages, 6 integration decisions - all inside one program, so calls are plain function calls and events are in-memory. Two questions at check-out (membership current? balance zero?) and one call out to Stripe.
plain_words.assumed: That everything runs as one deployable, so nothing needs a message queue yet, and that an in-memory event lost in a crash is re-derived by the next nightly run.
plain_words.riskiest: If the scheduled jobs become a separate program, two events start crossing a process boundary with no delivery guarantee, and late fees may silently stop accruing.
